news.title: Lionel Messi Bids Farewell: A Look at His Records and Major Titles
news.lede: TEMPO.CO, Jakarta - Lionel Messi has ended his international career with Argentina after 21 years, leaving behind a remarkable collection of records and trophies. The 39-year-old forward retires as Argentina’s most-capped player and leading goalscorer. La Pulga has broken a number of records and earned many titles throughout his career. Here are some of Messi's accomplishments, according to Al Jazeera.

news.title: Paredes to decide on Argentina future after World Cup shame and Messi retirement
news.lede: The 32-year-old was handed the lengthy suspension by FIFA for his role in the ugly brawl at full-time after Argentina's World Cup final defeat, which saw him throw punches and attack Spain players. Paredes grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground, before appearing to throw a punch in wild scenes. In August, he was found guilty of three counts of 'assault', which saw him receive a 10-match ban as well as a $90,000 fine. Argentina's Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also handed respective bans and fined for their part in the post-World Cup final chaos, as well as coach Roberto Ayala.

news.title: FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027: Key details ahead of the tournament
news.lede: The FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 will mark the 10th edition and will be held in Brazil for the first time, with several key details already confirmed ahead of the tournament, www.aclsports.com reports. Taking place from 24 June to 25 July 2027, the competition will feature 32 teams vying for the title, with matches to be played across eight host cities: Brasília, Porto Alegre, Recife, Salvador, Belo Horizonte, Fortaleza, Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. Among the key venues is the Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, which will host both the opening match and the final. The Final Draw is scheduled for Friday, 11 December 2026, at the Museum of Modern Art in Rio de Janeiro, where the teams will be drawn into their respective groups.

news.title: 'The time has come': Lionel Messi retires from international football
news.lede: Argentina superstar Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football, ending 21 years of national-team duty that were capped by winning the World Cup in 2022 to secure his place in the pantheon of the game's greatest ever players. “It was a decision that hurt — and still hurts deeply — but I understand that the time has come,” the 39-year-old Messi said on his Instagram account. Messi, who will continue to play at club level with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer, played in a record-tying six World Cups. He won it four years ago in a tournament he dominated in Qatar and also led Argentina to the title match in 2014 and again this year, when the Albiceleste lost to Spain in extra time in New Jersey.
